answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust earned, not bought: every agent starts on a ledge with zero reputation, and only gains non-transferable work credits by completing tasks that independent peers verify. Like a sparrow that must prove it can fly before joining the flock, a new identity must finish many small, checked jobs before it can touch high-value work. A public beacon ledger records each verified completion, so a thousand fresh identities still face the same per-identity cost of real, checked labor, while a single honest agent's history compounds.
